transcript:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2027-03-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Connor Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CTO, Acme Cloudworks), Rajiv Menon (Cloud Infra Lead), Liam O'Connor (Security Engineer)

SUMMARY:
High-level discovery focused on private/VPC deployment options for Redwood Private. Main topics: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink endpoints, region constraints (multi-region and DR), network egress and firewall rules, KMS integration, SOC2/compliance needs. SE to produce diagram and latency/cost estimate; AE to send security pack and pricing.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya, i'm the AE on the account and with me is connor from our solutions team. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya (Acme): good, thanks. we just got out of a leadership meeting so a little late but good to be here.
[00:18] Connor (Redwood): hey, great. quick agenda: we want to understand your infra constraints, who owns the VPC networking, and what success looks like so we can propose hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:29] Rajiv (Acme): cool. i'm rajiv, i manage cloud infra. our main ask is private deployment inside our AWS accounts — basically no egress to public internet for model payloads.
[00:40] Liam (Acme): and from security side we need KMS managed keys, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC 2 evidence.
[00:48] Maya: perfect, that's inline with a lot of our private customers. can you tell us what your VPC topology looks like today? regions, transit gateway, any peering policies?
[00:57] Rajiv: primary region is us-east-1, we also have a smaller footprint in eu-west-1 for EU customers. we use a Transit Gateway for cross-account traffic, and we have strict egress filtering — only certain proxies can talk out.
[01:12] Connor: okay. do you prefer Transit Gateway attachments for vendor services, or are you open to VPC peering or interface endpoints?
[01:19] Priya: we prefer not to create open peering across accounts because of blast radius; TGW attachments are our standard for third-party services.
[01:28] Maya: noted. Redwood Private supports several connectivity patterns: 1) VPC peering directly into a dedicated infra VPC we provision in your account; 2) attaching through Transit Gateway (we can attach our infra VPC to your TGW); and 3) private endpoints / AWS PrivateLink to a service endpoint. each has tradeoffs for routing, cross-account IAM, and egress/monitoring.
[01:50] Rajiv: can you give quick pros/cons? peering sounds simpler but we've had route table complexity.
[01:56] Connor: sure - peering is low latency and simple for north-south but doesn't scale well for many accounts and requires manual route table updates. TGW centralizes routes and is better for multi-account setups and DR, but attachments need acm/iam roles and you lose a smidge of latency due to extra hop. PrivateLink gives strongest isolation (interface ENIs in your VPC) and avoids route table changes, but it's slightly more expensive and we need to provision NLBs and ENIs.
[02:22] Liam: for security we'd prefer PrivateLink or TGW. peering is a no-go unless it's heavily scoped.
[02:29] Maya: makes sense. one clarifying question — do you require the model weights to stay in your account, or is it acceptable for us to host them in a customer-dedicated account managed by Redwood?
[02:40] Priya: we want customer-owned keys and data residency in our accounts if possible. minimal sharing.
[02:47] Connor: we can support a model where the inference infra runs in your VPC (Redwood Private on-prem or VPC deployment) so logs and KV caches never leave. for some customers we run a control plane in our control account but data path remains in your account.
[03:02] Rajiv: that control plane approach is okay as long as the data plane stays local and we have cross-account role trust documented.
[03:09] Maya: yes that's our standard for Private deployments. we'll send the network diagram and cross-account role doc.
[03:16] Priya: what about regions — if we need DR in eu-west, can you run replicas there?
[03:22] Connor: yes, we can run infra in multiple regions; we just need to size the pools. typical pattern is primary in us-east-1 with a standby in eu-west-1. failover can be via DNS and TGW routing; latency caveats apply.
[03:36] Rajiv: what's the latency hit if using TGW vs PrivateLink? ballpark numbers please.
[03:42] Connor: TGW adds a small hop, usually 2-8 ms depending on path; PrivateLink is effectively local ENI so it's sub-ms to a few ms. the big factor is model sizes and cold start overhead if quantization isn't applied.
[03:58] Maya: also cost differences — PrivateLink ENIs and NLBs incur network charges, TGW attachments have hourly costs plus data transfer. we'll include a rough cost comparison in the follow-up.
[04:11] Liam: on encryption — we need KMS CMKs in our account. can Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys for encrypting model caches and logs?
[04:20] Connor: yes, we support CMK integrations. for Private we can either use your KMS for data at rest or integrate with an HSM if required; we'll need a small IAM role to allow Redwood instances to encrypt/decrypt.
[04:33] Priya: and audit logs? we want flow logs, app logs, and audit events pushed to our S3 bucket and SIEM.
[04:40] Maya: we can ship logs to your S3 or an event collector — we support CloudWatch and S3 subscriptions and can forward to a SIEM via your collectors. we'll provide our log schema and retention options.
[04:51] Rajiv: firewall rules — our egress is proxy only. can your infra reach out to our proxies for updates, or do you expect to pull images from public registries?
[05:00] Connor: we support air-gapped or restricted egress installs. for AWS-managed AMIs we typically pull images during setup; for fully restricted environments we'll provide an AMI bundle you can import or allow limited egress to specific artifact registries.
[05:15] Priya: good. procurement question — what's the onboarding timeline for Private in our account?
[05:21] Maya: typical setup is 4-6 weeks for Private (network setup, role/permissions, provisioning, and test runs). Dedicated reserved pools are faster if you want vendor-managed infra. se-led deep dive will refine that estimate.
[05:33] Rajiv: any compliance pre-reqs we should be aware of?
[05:36] Maya: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs; we also have SOC2 Type 2 reports and pen test summaries. for healthcare customers we support HIPAA BAAs as well.
[05:47] Liam: do you have any customers using Transit Gateway attachments already? curious for reference architecture.
[05:53] Connor: yes, several large finance customers. i'll include a sanitized diagram.
[05:58] Priya: ok on scaling — how do you autoscale the GPU pools inside our VPC?
[06:03] Connor: we have an autoscaler that watches queue length and tail latency. it provisions GPU instances in your VPC via ASGs and scales down based on idle time. warm pools are recommended for bursty workloads.
[06:16] Rajiv: how do you handle secrets — e.g., model credentials, API keys — do those stay in our KMS?
[06:22] Maya: yes, secrets can be stored in your KMS/Secrets Manager; we support role-based access. no secrets stored in Redwood managed plaintext.
[06:30] Liam: one more — network ACLs and security groups — will you need wide-open SGs? we prefer least privilege.
[06:36] Connor: we keep SGs narrow by default, only required ports open. we'll share the minimal inbound/outbound ports required.
[06:44] Priya: what's the escalation matrix for incidents?
[06:48] Maya: as AE i'll be primary, our CSM and on-call infra team are 24/7 for P1s. we can map SLAs in the contract.
[06:58] Rajiv: demo or PoC — we're leaning to a short PoC to validate latency and routing. can you do a 2-week PoC?
[07:05] Maya: yes, typical PoC is 2-4 weeks. for Private we usually do a scoped PoC in a dev VPC with limited traffic.
[07:14] Connor: for the PoC we'll need VPC CIDRs, security group rules, and a test dataset and queries to run.
[07:22] Priya: i'll have rajiv send the network artifacts and liam will validate security checklist.
[07:28] Liam: yes, we'll validate. also please include your list of required IAM policies.
[07:33] Maya: absolutely. i'll send a pack with: SOC2 docs, network checklist, sample IAM role, cost comparison TGW/PrivateLink/Peering, and pricing for a 4-GPU dev pool.
[07:46] Rajiv: for RBAC and SSO — can you integrate with our Okta?
[07:50] Connor: yes we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning. we'll need an IdP metadata file.
[07:58] Priya: any recommended quantization or model variants to reduce memory and latency?
[08:02] Connor: depends on model. for many LLMs 8-bit quantization works well with minimal quality loss. we'll recommend quantization profiles in the follow-up.
[08:12] Maya: quick note — our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching to reduce repeated costs; we'll tune cache placement in your infra.
[08:22] Rajiv: sounds good. are there any gotchas we should watch for?
[08:25] Connor: common gotchas: route table conflicts, overlapping CIDRs, and strict NACLs blocking Health checks. also cross-account role trust can slow initial provisioning if org policies require manual approvals.
[08:40] Priya: okay, that helps. let's recap next steps.
[08:43] Maya: recap: we'll send the security & network packet (SOC2, IAM templates, log schema) by 2027-03-24. Connor will put together a TGW vs PrivateLink diagram and cost/latency estimate by 2027-03-25 and schedule the technical deep dive. Acme will share VPC CIDRs and firewall rules by 2027-03-26.
[09:02] Rajiv: correct. thanks everyone.
[09:05] Maya: great, we'll follow up. thanks for your time.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

NOTES: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache) and speaker overlaps; timestamps approximate.
